conclusion: Attempt 1 produced one ticket-success candidate: wideproj1024 exceeded the immutable baseline at all five aligned late checkpoints for Combined-X, Combined-O, and aggregate, with final-five means 0.504, 0.232, and 0.524 versus 0.358, 0.150, and 0.437. Corrected LR decay improved both Combined sides but regressed aggregate/offensive strength, while batch256 improved Combined-O and Defensive-O but regressed Combined-X and aggregate. No candidate is opponent-pool ready because neither Combined side achieved the required sustained 0.60 on both sides; wideproj1024 is the best new warmup checkpoint but should be replicated and improved specifically on Combined-O before self-play.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Correcting the baseline's accidentally rising learning-rate expression to a true 3e-4-to-1e-4 decay would improve late Combined-policy strength on both learner sides while preserving overall heuristic performance.

results_insights.insight: True LR decay materially improved Combined-X throughout the aligned late window.
Combined-O also improved, with paired episode length rising from 9.650 to 10.182, consistent with somewhat more contested weak-side play.
The candidate failed ticket condition 1 because aggregate performance regressed despite both Combined-side gains.
The aggregate regression is strongly associated with lost Offensive-X competence, contradicting the preservation part of the hypothesis.

The change improved Defensive-O, but this local benefit did not transfer to broad offense or Combined-X strength.
